title: The Rust Programming Language: Object-Oriented Programming Features
design: Favor traits and composition instead of inherited class hierarchies.
limitation: Conceptual guidance; not evidence of runtime correctness.
acceptance: Prove two heterogeneous modules implement one object-safe interface.

title: The Rust Reference: Dyn Compatibility
design: Keep runtime module interface dyn-compatible (no generic methods or associated constants).
limitation: Runtime dispatch does not enforce operating-system permissions.
acceptance: Compile polymorphic test implementations as Box<dyn RuntimeModule>.

title: RustBelt: Securing the Foundations of the Rust Programming Language
design: Keep unsafe and foreign-function boundaries outside core domain types.
limitation: Formal result does not prove each third-party dependency or device driver safe.
acceptance: Review unsafe dependencies and keep device I/O isolated.
contributors: Ralf Jung; Jacques-Henri Jourdan; Robbert Krebbers; Derek Dreyer

title: Local-first software: You own your data, in spite of the cloud
design: Prioritize local data ownership and offline functionality before optional synchronization.
limitation: Discusses CRDTs as potential tools; does not mandate sync or CRDT usage now.
acceptance: Offline create/read/export work with network disabled.
contributors: Martin Kleppmann; Adam Wiggins; Peter van Hardenberg; Mark McGranaghan

title: Ratatui TestBackend
design: Use memory-backed terminal frames and keyboard event replay for deterministic UI tests.
limitation: Current reference may describe a newer Ratatui version than this workspace's 0.29 dependency.
acceptance: Pin dependency; verify API and capture small-terminal snapshots.

title: embedded-hal 1.0.0
design: Use hardware abstraction traits where peripheral protocols fit; keep Linux-specific GPIO separate.
limitation: Embedded HAL traits do not replace Linux userspace GPIO drivers or cover SDR.
acceptance: Build fake GPIO inputs before hardware tests.

title: Linux GPIO character device v2 userspace API
design: Use kernel-supported GPIO requests instead of sysfs and ad-hoc bit banging.
limitation: Linux-specific and dependent on kernel + device capabilities.
acceptance: Require permission-denied, disconnect, and debounce tests.

title: gpsd JSON protocol: TPV and SKY
design: Model optional GNSS measurements, explicit fix quality, and sample freshness.
limitation: Receiver and gpsd presence are not guaranteed; TPV can omit location fields.
acceptance: Replay no-fix, stale-fix and malformed payload fixtures.

title: RFC 7946: The GeoJSON Format
design: Use standards-based GeoJSON import/export with WGS84 coordinates.
limitation: Format specification is not a routing engine or a tile licensing grant.
acceptance: Reject invalid coordinates and preserve geometry types.
contributors: H. Butler; M. Daly; A. Doyle; S. Gillies; S. Hagen; T. Schaub

title: OpenStreetMap copyright and ODbL license
design: Track map-data provenance and attribution requirements in offline bundles.
limitation: ODbL applies to data; tiles and styles can have different terms.
acceptance: Every imported map bundle records source/license/attribution.

title: OpenStreetMap Foundation tile usage policy
design: Never bulk-prefetch official OSM raster tiles for Rust-Boy offline maps.
limitation: Provider policy is distinct from OSM database license and can change.
acceptance: Offline map test uses user-supplied, permitted tile bundles only.

title: Bluetooth Core Specification 6.2
design: Use explicit pairing, connection security and known peripheral capabilities.
limitation: Bluetooth pairing alone does not equal application-layer peer trust.
acceptance: Manual pairing and peer identity tests; no automatic discovery.

title: btleplug Rust BLE Central library
design: Consider platform-specific BLE adapter behind a host-only trait.
limitation: Library and backend support vary; no implementation approval yet.
acceptance: Mock BLE central callbacks and verify cancellation.

title: serialport-rs cross-platform API
design: Abstract serial enumeration and read-only device sessions.
limitation: Some platform backends and native libraries may require extra dependencies.
acceptance: Test manual port selection, unplug, timeout and cancellation.

title: RFC 9180: Hybrid Public Key Encryption
design: Evaluate standard cryptographic envelopes for future trusted local communications.
limitation: HPKE alone does not provide a complete authenticated messaging protocol or key lifecycle.
acceptance: Threat model and independent protocol review before sending messages.
contributors: R. Barnes; K. Bhargavan; B. Lipp; C. Wood

title: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework
design: Apply threat modeling, dependency hygiene, testing and change provenance.
limitation: A practice framework, not proof of security certification.
acceptance: Document dependency audit, reviewed risks and release approvals.
contributors: Murugiah Souppaya; Karen Scarfone; Donna Dodson

title: SLSA specification v1.2
design: Record build provenance and improve artifact integrity incrementally.
limitation: Do not claim a SLSA level merely by producing a GitHub workflow.
acceptance: Validate release provenance with known source and builder identities.

title: W3C WCAG 2.2 Recommendation
design: Borrow keyboard access, contrast and reduced-motion accessibility criteria.
limitation: Primarily a web content standard; terminal-specific usability needs separate testing.
acceptance: Keyboard-only journeys, screen-size tests and readable status without color alone.

title: RFC 8259 JSON interchange
design: Use versioned JSON data interchange and strictly validate inputs.
limitation: JSON alone provides neither schema governance nor data authenticity.
acceptance: Reject malformed data and incompatible schema versions.

title: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3: Guide to OT Security
design: Maintain read-only field instrumentation and separate control from observation.
limitation: Relevant to OT-adjacent environments; not permission to operate infrastructure.
acceptance: Ensure sensor/radio modules cannot actuate external systems by default.

title: LoRaWAN L2 1.0.4 Specification
design: Compare licensed LoRaWAN device constraints during transport selection.
limitation: LoRaWAN is not interchangeable with Meshtastic point-to-point mesh; do not assume interoperability.
acceptance: Choose and document a specific transport before protocol code.

title: NIST SP 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
design: Require explicit peer authorization rather than trusting proximity.
limitation: Enterprise design guidance; adapt proportionally to a personal field device.
acceptance: Deny untrusted peer messages and show consent state.
contributors: Scott Rose; Oliver Borchert; Stu Mitchell; Sean Connelly

title: FAA ADS-B installation overview
design: Distinguish 1090ES and 978 MHz UAT in receiver/decoder capability planning.
limitation: Airborne equipage guidance is not a decoder implementation or authorization to transmit.
acceptance: Receive-only data fixtures distinguish source channel and uncertainty.

title: SoapySDR Rust bindings documentation
design: Consider a receiver-only abstraction over supported SDR hardware.
limitation: FFI and native drivers require per-platform auditing; TX APIs must not be enabled by default.
acceptance: Mock IQ source; document library and driver prerequisites.

title: The Rust Programming Language: trait objects
design: Use Box<dyn Trait> for heterogeneous internal modules; generics for homogeneous hot paths.
limitation: Trait objects are runtime polymorphism, not a stable cross-language plugin ABI.
acceptance: Test two module types under a shared host without dynamic library loading.

title: QuickCheck: A lightweight tool for random testing of Haskell programs
design: Use property-based generators and invariants to stress schema, event and permission contracts beyond handpicked fixtures.
limitation: Published for Haskell, not a guarantee that a specific Rust test generator or harness is correctly applied.
acceptance: Introduce generator-based tests for event ordering, corrupted payloads and round-trip storage.

title: Energy Efficiency across Programming Languages: How do Energy, Time, and Memory Relate?
contributors: Rui Pereira; Marco Couto; Francisco Ribeiro; Rui Rua; Jácome Cunha; João Paulo Fernandes; João Saraiva
design: Measure latency, peak memory and power on actual wearable hardware; do not optimize from language choice alone.
limitation: Benchmark tasks and language-level comparisons do not predict Rust-Boy battery life or SDR load.
acceptance: Record idle/active power and CPU baselines on selected Raspberry Pi, with reproducible workloads.

title: Bluetooth Low Energy Mesh Networks: Survey of Communication and Security Protocols
contributors: Muhammad Rizwan Ghori; Tat-Chee Wan; Gian Chand Sodhy
design: Evaluate topology, broadcast behavior, cryptographic trust and provisioning before choosing a BLE mesh implementation.
limitation: Survey literature does not imply interoperation with a specific BLE central crate or Meshtastic device.
acceptance: Compare two selected candidate transports using threat model, throughput and energy criteria.

title: Bluetooth Low Energy Mesh: Applications, Considerations and Current State-of-the-Art
contributors: Iynkaran Natgunanathan; Niroshinie Fernando; Seng W. Loke; Charitha Weerasuriya
design: Treat wearables and IoT meshes as constrained systems with range, energy and operational trade-offs.
limitation: Review across use cases does not validate Rust-Boy hardware or specific link budget.
acceptance: Set peer density, battery budget, range and reconnection fixtures before selecting radio hardware.

title: Bringing Up OpenSky: A Large-scale ADS-B Sensor Network for Research
contributors: Matthias Schäfer; Martin Strohmeier; Vincent Lenders; Ivan Martinovic; Matthias Wilhelm
design: Model aircraft observations as received sensor measurements with coverage, receiver source and timestamp, not authoritative global tracks.
limitation: Research network deployment does not establish GNSS accuracy or validate a local dongle decoder.
acceptance: Compare recorded receive-only ADS-B fixtures with known decoder outputs and explicit coverage gaps.
